result.text:
"Hackers Leak Data From Thousands of Visa, Mastercard & JPMorgan Customers After Third-Party Vendor Breaches"

➡️ A ransomware group known as n0n leaked customer data tied to Visa, Mastercard & JPMorgan Chase on Thursday, November 19, 2026, after its 48-hour extortion deadline passed. All 3 financial institutions confirmed that hackers obtained the files by breaching outside service providers rather than breaking into the banks' or card networks' internal computer systems.

➡️ Visa confirmed that its incident originated at a third-party vendor operating in the Asia-Pacific region & has since been contained. While the leaked files reportedly include member profiles, full names, email addresses, mobile numbers & travel or dining booking details for premium cardholders, Visa emphasized that core payment networks were untouched & No credit or debit card numbers were compromised.

➡️ Mastercard reported that the exposure was restricted to a limited subset of cardholders enrolled in a specific benefit program, confirming that customers can continue using their cards normally without interruption. Cybersecurity researchers warned that exposed contact details from loyalty & benefit platforms still leave affected cardholders vulnerable to targeted phishing scams.

➡️ JPMorgan Chase stated that outside vendors holding marketing files were targeted, exposing roughly 16,000 customer email addresses tied to its invitation-only Reserve card program alongside some phone numbers, account IDs & more than 100 bank employee email addresses. The bank confirmed it will contact impacted individuals directly & offer complimentary credit monitoring support where appropriate.

➡️ Officials across all 3 companies stressed that the data leak has caused No disruptions to payment processing or daily banking operations. JPMorgan Chase also confirmed that the vendor cyberattack has No connection to the widespread online banking & transaction outage that affected Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo & Zelle on November 16, 2026, which was caused by a temporary software bug in on-premise hardware systems.

NAND prices plunge 20% in just two weeks!

According to Overclock3D, NAND flash spot prices have dropped approximately 20% over a two-week period, raising hopes of lower SSD prices after a year of rising storage costs.

The decline is particularly sharp for certain memory products:

- 512Gb NAND wafer prices are down 32% quarter-over-quarter, reaching $14.30.
- 1Tb #NAND prices have fallen 19%, reaching $24.90.

The slowdown in PC and smartphone demand, combined with growing competition from Chinese manufacturer YMTC, is putting pressure on the consumer NAND market.

Further declines are expected. Bank of America forecasts consumer NAND contract prices could fall another 5–10% in Q1 2027.

However, don't expect #SSD prices to drop overnight. Lower component costs take time to reach retail products, and enterprise SSD demand remains strong.
